observations: Bare automatic transmission bell housing and torque converter shown on dirt ground, disassembled in later photo
External casing shows wear, oxidation, and old fluid residue
A small rectangular data/tag label is visible on the case in photo 1 but text is not legible
No fluid pan, no wiring harness/mechatronic unit, no dipstick visible in any photo
Torque converter shown separated from bell housing in photo 2, splines and converter hub visible but no seal or bushing close-up
No VIN plate, no serial number, no engine bay or vehicle context shown

identity.kind: automatic transmission/gearbox assembly (seller claims compatibility with Mercedes M272 engine)

claims.evidence: No legible model/serial plate in any photo; tag visible in photo 1 is unreadable, so 'M272' compatibility cannot be confirmed from images
Sales statement, not a verifiable physical claim

risks.risk: Internal gearbox condition (clutch packs, bands, valve body) unknown; could be seized, damaged gears, or shift problems
risks.proof: Video of gearbox being manually turned/rotated at input shaft, or bench/stand test clip showing shifting or fluid drain showing no metal shavings

risks.risk: Torque converter lock-up clutch and seal condition unknown; converter could be worn or leaking
risks.proof: Close-up photo/video of converter hub seal area and a shake test for internal rattle/fluid leakage

risks.risk: Mechatronic/solenoid unit and wiring harness missing from photos; required for a 'complete' claim
risks.proof: Photo showing mechatronic unit attached with connector and wiring intact
risks.if_unproven: priced as incomplete unit lacking electronic control module

risks.risk: No confirmation this gearbox actually matches M272 engine bellhousing/bolt pattern
risks.proof: Clear photo of stamped part number or tag, matched against Mercedes parts catalog
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic used transmission of unconfirmed fitment

risks.risk: Possible water/dirt ingress from being stored on bare ground outdoors
risks.proof: Close-up of input/output shaft seals and interior cavity for rust or debris

proof_requests: Clear, well-lit close-up of the data/serial tag/plate so model and fitment can be confirmed
Video of the gearbox being tested on a bench or in a vehicle, showing shifting or at minimum free rotation without grinding
Photo of the mechatronic/solenoid unit and wiring harness, confirming 'complete' claim
Close-up of torque converter seal/hub area and listen/shake test for internal rattle
Photo of fluid drained from pan (if available) to check for metal debris
response.reason: This is clearly identifiable by type as a used automatic transmission assembly with torque converter, but no claims of completeness, fitment to M272, or working condition can be verified from the photos, so it must be priced at worst case as an untested, possibly incomplete used gearbox core.
